sections.title: Packaging settings for installation
sections.what: Describes the package name, version, author placeholders, supported Python versions from 3.9 upward, the required libraries, and the capex-watcher command that calls main.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app be installed like a standard Python package.

summary: Packaging settings that describe the app as an installable Python package and create a command named capex-watcher.
purpose: Lets the app be installed as a package with one command, in addition to the run scripts.
why: Likely reason: standard practice for Python projects that want an installable command.
how: Reads the README text and the requirements file, then declares the name, version, supported Python versions, required libraries, and the command that calls main.
outputs: Package metadata and an installed command when the package is installed.
risks: Author, email, and URL fields still hold placeholder text. The README file must exist or installation fails. Development tools in requirements also get installed as required packages.
debug: If installation fails with a missing file, check that README.md and requirements.txt sit next to this file. If the command is not found after install, check that the entry point points to main.main.
